Bangladesh says legal process complete to secure Hasina’s return, decision rests with India: reports
 India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision on handing her over
 Updated - November 14, 2026 07:57 pm IST - Dhaka 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Sheikh Hasina. File
 | Photo Credit: Reuters
 Bangladesh has completed all legal procedures required to secure the return of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from India, and the next step rests with New Delhi, Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026), according to local media reports.
 Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties 
 “We have completed everything required from our side as part of the legal process. What they [India] will do is up to them,” Mr. Asaduzzaman told reporters after an event at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka, according to Prothom Alo .
 The Minister said Ms. Hasina would return through legal means and her extradition under the bilateral treaty would itself constitute a legal process.
 What are the legal compulsions and political hurdles in Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh? | Explained Regarding whether she would be entitled to appeal her death sentence, Mr. Asaduzzaman said she would not have that opportunity under the relevant law, Dhaka Tribune reported.
 When asked whether India had discussed sending Ms. Hasina to a third country with Bangladesh, the Minister said the Indian government would be able to answer that question, Prothom Alo reported.
 Bangladesh has been seeking Ms. Hasina’s extradition from India after she fled the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
 Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal convicted Ms. Hasina in November 2025 for her role in the crackdown on protesters during the uprising.
 After Bangladesh rules out passport for Hasina, India says ‘travel document’ needed Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Ms. Hasina has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
 Bangladesh’s demand for Ms. Hasina’s extradition has continued even after the interim government that succeeded her administration handed over power in February to an elected government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
 India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision on handing her over.
 ‘Extradition legal matter’
 On Friday (November 13), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.
 He further said: “India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh.”
 Dhaka wants Hasina extradited under prisoner exchange Ms. Hasina has said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December. She made the announcement during an audio-only virtual press conference with journalists organised in New Delhi on August 5.
 Bilateral ties strained
 The event drew a sharp reaction from Dhaka; Bangladesh’s Foreign Ministry said it was “outraged” that Ms. Hasina had been allowed to interact with the media in New Delhi despite Dhaka conveying its concerns to the Indian government in advance.
 India, however, distanced itself from the event, saying it was organised by a private media entity and that the government had “no involvement whatsoever” in it.
 Dhaka has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Mr. Rahman, saying New Delhi should expedite her handover and return other fugitives sought by Bangladesh to create a conducive environment for the visit.
 Consular dialogue postponed
 The India-Bangladesh consular dialogue was scheduled for next week, but it has been postponed.
 Ms. Hasina has no legal option left but to face execution of her death sentence, the International Crimes Tribunal’s chief prosecutor Md. Aminul Islam said earlier this week, rejecting the possibility of issuing her a passport or travel document.
 His remarks came a day after Ms. Hasina, through a London-based legal chamber, approached the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi seeking a new passport and national identity card.
 Bangladesh’s Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed had then said the government was examining the authenticity and legal grounds of applications submitted by Ms. Hasina.
 However, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir reiterated that Dhaka would seek her return from India only through an existing extradition treaty.
